data.claim: contended inverts waiting.wait_for_graph, which recomputes a waiter's edges from its STALE recorded ask (lease.waiting globs); a waiter that narrowed its globs after the refused widening is still named for the holder whose file it gave up.
data.falsifier: test_a_waiter_that_narrowed_away_is_not_held_contended asserts 'T2' not in contended(...)[T1] after T2 narrows src/b.py,src/a.py back to src/b.py -- it FAILED before the fix (contended=={'T1':['T2']}) and PASSES after.
data.mechanism: update --globs wider is refused and records lease.waiting with the refused globs; update --globs narrower succeeds (retarget keeps the same lease.event) so the recorded ask stays stale; wait_for_graph recomputes from the stale ask; contended inverts to holder->waiters; the heartbeat surfaces it as a false YIELD REQUESTED.
data.probe: Write the regression test, run it on the unfixed code, then after the fix.
data.probe_output: FAILED tests/test_lease_yield_disjoint_waiter.py (contended=={'T1':['T2']}), then after filtering contended by current-glob overlap: 1 passed.
data.question: Does leasebreak.contended name a waiter whose current globs no longer overlap the holder?
